correctness.rationale: The product characters give the stated row kernel, whose absolute mass is attained by its real sign. For each coordinate, its centered row contribution has mean zero and support {-1,b}; the secant formula for a convex function at zero is monotone in b. The rare row maximizes b coordinatewise, and increasing a rare-atom probability decreases b. Independence allows this comparison after conditioning on the other summands. Negative row mass is half the difference between absolute mass and total mass one. The all-zero configuration gives the limiting negative mass n-1 as all rare probabilities vanish; the positive-probability all-one configuration makes the open-cube bound strict for n>=2. The fair minimum follows from even-sign parity and the central binomial identity. The binomial truncation uses the exact strict negativity cutoff, and the Gaussian and Poisson limits use bounded second moments at their respective normalizations. The Poisson derivative is negative in each open interval (j,j+1), and the adjacent masses agree but derivatives differ at each integer. The case n=1 is the identity. An independent weighted conditional-mean construction checked all 54 rows in four profiles and reproduced norm 203/75 and negative mass 64/75 at the cited asymmetric profile.
residual_risks: The finite checks establish only the enumerated profiles, not the general comparison or asymptotic regimes.
